issues.body:
Carried forward from rounds 3/4 at nit severity; re-derived independently and I agree it is not blocking.

The two new rows at :1426-1440 inject a `refuse` callable, so they never exercise the `require is None` branch at :101-103. That branch is not untested in practice: `_load_workflow_yaml()` is called unconditionally at module scope (:109), so it runs on every single invocation of this watchdog, live and self-test alike. A mutant deleting `from yaml_dependency import require_yaml` leaves `require` as None, `require(...)` raises TypeError at IMPORT time, and the script dies before any assertion runs — the mutant is killed loudly in every lane.

What remains is only a failure-SHAPE wart: `except (ImportError, RuntimeError)` at :105 does not include TypeError, so that particular death is an unhandled traceback rather than the structured `(None, exc)` path the docstring advertises the loader preserves. The live consumer at :1015 is unaffected either way (it raises AlarmError when `yaml is None`), so there is no fail-open here and nothing gate-relevant. Recording it so the next reader does not re-derive it.
issues.fix_hint:
Optional, and safe to defer. Either widen the tuple so an un-set `require` also lands on the structured path:

    except (ImportError, RuntimeError, TypeError) as exc:

or add one row that drives the real default branch by making the genuine import fail:

    import sys as _sys
    _saved = _sys.modules.pop("yaml_dependency", None)
    _sys.modules["yaml_dependency"] = None  # forces ImportError on `from ... import`
    try:
        default_path = _load_workflow_yaml()
    finally:
        _sys.modules.pop("yaml_dependency", None)
        if _saved is not None:
            _sys.modules["yaml_dependency"] = _saved
    chk("yaml loader takes the structured path when the helper module itself cannot be imported",
        default_path[0] is None and isinstance(default_path[1], ImportError))
issues.title: TypeError is outside the loader's except tuple, so the `require is None` default path would die with an opaque traceback rather than the structured detector path

verdict.summary:
Re-verified from scratch rather than inheriting round 4. No blocker or major found; the single carried-forward nit is unchanged, hence "stagnant" (same finding, same severity, materially unchanged diff).

What I checked and confirmed:

1. SUITE ENROLMENT. yaml_dependency.py:87 spells `if len(sys.argv) == 2 and sys.argv[1] == "--self-test":`; worker-live.sh:1043's discovery ERE (third alternative `sys\.argv\[[^]]+\][[:space:]]*==[[:space:]]*"--self-test"`, with the `^[[:space:]]*[^#].*` prefix satisfied) matches, and selftest-suite.txt:66 enrols it. Both arms of the manifest cross-check (enrolled-but-entrypointless, advertising-but-unenrolled) are satisfied.

2. SPARSE-CHECKOUT / REQUIRED_FILES, all 13 blocks re-walked. Every job that EXECUTES a converted consumer gained scripts/yaml_dependency.py. The exact-equality assertions hold as sets: dispatch-tick-floor.py:1669, dispatch-stall-alert.py:1152, groom-mint-alert.py:1765, regate-sweep.py:2818 (6 files + 1 dir = 7 sparse lines). The subset-direction ones (ci-latency-alert.py:2847, metrics-alert.py:1075, ratelimit-alert.py:1063) hold too. groom-mint-alert.py:1763's _REQUIRED_READS equality is satisfied because :1751 `_require()`s every REQUIRED_FILES entry. Correct omissions: backfill-provenance.yml:69 is the tomllib `resolve` job (its --self-test runs at :174 under the FULL checkout at :123); dispatch.yml:1583 runs only dispatch-secrets-guard.py, which keeps a bare `import yaml` at :319 and reads worker-pr.py statically; dispatch.yml:2287 and groom-sweep.yml:836 host unconverted scripts.

3. sys.path. Every converted site resolves `yaml_dependency` because the runner invokes `python3 <root>/<script> --self-test` (worker-live.sh:1225), so sys.path[0] is the scripts dir.
